notes:
The Vocia MS-1e is a 1U rack-mount "message processor" (networked paging/messaging server) in Biamp's Vocia PA/voice-evacuation system line — not an AV signal-routing box, so most rear ports are network/control rather than audio/video signal I/O.

Sources cross-checked: (1) official "Vocia MS-1e Installation and Operation Guide" (rev. 28JAN2025, downloads.biamp.com/assets/docs/default-source/manuals/vocia_ms-1e_may19.pdf) — used as primary source for the port list because it has an explicit numbered rear-panel legend; (2) official Data Sheet VOCDS-422-2105-EN-R1, May 2021 (https://downloads.biamp.com/assets/docs/default-source/data-sheets/biamp_data_sheet_vocia_ms-1e_may21.pdf).

Discrepancy found between the two official documents: the 2021 data sheet's rear-panel line art shows an HDMI-labeled port (two stacked HDMI jacks) between the LAN ports and the USB group; the newer (2025) installation manual's rear-panel diagram shows no HDMI at all in that location (just ventilation holes) and instead shows an unlabeled VGA-shaped D-sub connector further right. I followed the newer, more detailed/labeled manual and omitted HDMI; flagging this so it can be re-verified against a physical unit or current Biamp support if precision matters.

Per Biamp's own manual text, the 4x USB-A ports and the unlabeled VGA-shaped D-sub port are explicitly called "Inactive" ("these ports are inactive at this time... connection of external devices to inactive ports is not required or recommended") — almost certainly leftover headers from the embedded-PC motherboard the appliance is built on. They are included here as physical connectors that exist on the chassis, but are non-functional per the manufacturer.

RS-232 port: labeled "RS-232/485" in the 2021 data sheet's back-panel artwork, but only "RS-232" in the 2025 manual's diagram/text (both show a female DB9). Modeled as connector "rs232" with accepts ["rs485"] to reflect the fuller labeling.

Ethernet port link speed (Fast/Gigabit) and USB version are not stated in either document, so grade was omitted for all RJ45 and USB-A ports.

Two rotary "Device ID" switches (MSB/LSB, hex 00–FF) are present on the rear panel for setting a unique unit ID — these are configuration dials, not signal/power connectors, so they were excluded from the port list.

Power: internal universal switching supply, 100–240VAC 50/60Hz via IEC inlet; consumption is listed as "<300W" in the data sheet vs. "max 350 watts" in the manual (minor inter-document discrepancy, not port-relevant). Dimensions: 1.75"H x 19"W x 17.5"D (1RU), ~12 lbs.
